articles.title: Alonso: "¿2027? Esta situación es la que es..."
articles.standfirst: El asturiano apenas pasó de 20 vueltas en el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán, mostró su frustración y mantiene esperanza en la mejora de Honda en el futuro
articles.summary: El asturiano apenas pasó de 20 vueltas en el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán, mostró su frustración y mantiene esperanza en la mejora de Honda en el futuro
articles.body: Fernando Alonso no cruzó la vuelta 22 del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán cuando tuvo que verse obligado a abandonar. También lo hizo un rato antes su compañero en Aston Martin, Lance Stroll. En el seno del equipo británico ya sabían que la cita caucásica no iba a ser más que una prueba de un coche aligerado y con algún retoque, pero los más de dos kilómetros de recta que atraviesan el Boulevard de Bakú también sacaron a la luz las debilidades del proyecto. Las principales son de Honda, el suministrador de motores. No existe más que una confirmación de unos problemas que no se solucionan y que dejan una papeleta difícil de cara al 2027. Tanto de un proyecto que tiene todo para pasar al frente como de su estrella, Fernando Alonso. No ha tomado una decisión y sabe lo que hay. "Es lo que es esta situación. Sabemos que hay cosas que se escapan de nuestro control y trabajamos para resolver los problemas", precisó el asturiano ante la prensa internacional. El de Oviedo mantiene la fe dentro de lo que cabe. "La falta de rendimiento es una cosa, pero sabemos lo que todo el mundo intenta mejorar. No ayudan, claro, los problemas de fiabilidad de cada semana si no tienes el kilometraje. Creo que estamos haciendo nuestra parte del trabajo, que consiste en ayudar al equipo a intentar entender cómo ganar velocidad en las curvas", explicó. Con mensaje a Honda. "Cuando pisamos el acelerador y estamos en la recta, tenemos que confiar en Honda y en que vaya mejorando cada vez más. Hemos dado un paso adelante con la mejora del motor. Pero no es suficiente y tenemos que seguir trabajando", agregó. En Bakú eso no ocurrió. Durante la carrera repitió que sufría problemas con el motor y terminó abandonando pese a que el equipo no detectaba lo mismo desde el muro. "No vi ninguna alarma. Todo funcionaba bien, pero empecé a perder mucho en la recta. Como 1,5 segundos. Era algo anómalo", recordó. Lo mejor es que llegan circuitos teóricamente favorables. "Si hay menos recta, mejor para nosotros. Pero sigues necesitando potencia", expresó sobre lo que vendrá en Malasia y Singapur. Con cautela hasta para el circuito urbano que llegará en 15 días. "Hasta allí lo necesitas. Budapest depende menos de la potencia que Singapur. Aunque la situación será mejor que en Monza y Bakú. Además, tenemos que hacerlo mejor como equipo", cerró.

articles.title: Así queda el Mundial de F1 tras el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán en Bakú
articles.standfirst: Antonelli hace una carrera de campeón
articles.summary: Antonelli hace una carrera de campeón
articles.body: Final del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán, y ya van 15. Un fin de semana en el que George Russell demostró una superioridad ante el resto y en el que aprovechó los errores de su compañero de equipo y líder del Mundial, recortándole 15 puntos. El británico suma así su tercera victoria de la temporada y mantiene viva la lucha por el Mundial, con un total de 261 puntos, a 63 puntos de su compañero, Kimi Antonelli. Max Verstappen acabó 2º, a una décima del de Mercedes y tras una intensa lucha que se llevó hasta línea de meta. Tras un fin de semana dando pasos adelante y mostrando ser el único capaz de 'ponerle los puntos sobre las íes' a Russell, el neerlandés tuvo problemas durante la Qualy, clasificando finalmente 8º. Aún y así, cambió todos los componentes de combustión, aunque sin penalización por tener recambios, y pudo ir adelantando posiciones hasta colocarse 3º, justo por detrás de Oscar Piastri, quien acabó cometiendo un error y regalándole la 2ª plaza a Verstappen. El último escalón del Pódium fue para Isack Hadjar, quien regresaba tras una dura lesión que le mantuvo fuera de combate tres Grandes Premios. Aún y así, el francés pudo ir dando pasos adelante durante todo el fin de semana y, tras clasificar 4º en parrilla y mantener una lucha con su compañero de equipo, Verstappen, el de Red Bull Racing acabó 3º en Bakú. Un error en la Q1 condenó a Kimi Antonelli a partir 16º en la carrera del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán. Aún y así, el italiano mantuvo la calma y, a pesar de perder posiciones en la salida, confió en su talento y en su monoplaza, aprovechándose de los infortunios de otros pilotos por delante de él y firmar un 5º puesto. Aunque no sea la remontada que le hubiera gustado y la que todo el mundo esperaba, Antonelli suma 12 puntos que le pueden dar el Mundial. Los problemas se le acumulan a Aston Martin y, en especial, a Honda, acabando con la paciencia del piloto español. El Bicampeón del Mundo tan solo completó 21 vueltas muy frustrantes y en las que se le vio claramente enfadado, ante la incapacidad hacerle frente a los rivales con su monoplaza. Además, a esto se le añade el desastre que ha supuesto el fin de semana en general. Partía con una sanción de 25 posiciones por cambiar su Unidad de Potencia, la cual se acabó rompiendo, haciendo que tuvieran que volver a montar el motor antiguo. Problemas que se suman y que van calando en el piloto español, cuya amenaza de acabar su historia con la Fórmula 1 cada vez se hace más latente. Con mejoras en su Williams, aunque tampoco como para lanzar cohetes, Carlos ha podido sacarle provecho y, tras meterse en Q3 y clasificar 9º, el madrileño tuvo que volver a tirar de talento para salvar un punto. Una sanción por bandera amarilla condenó a Sainz a salir desde la 14ª posición, la cuál acabó siendo un desastre. Perdió varias posiciones en la salida y no tuvo más remedio que remontar, aprovechándose, eso sí, de los diversos incidentes que se formaron por delante. Finalmente pudo pasar a Hulkenberg a menos de 5 vueltas para el final, firmando así un 10º puesto. Parecía que este iba a ser un Mundial a 4 entre los dos Mercedes y los dos Ferrari. Sin embargo, poco a poco los de la escudería italiana han ido diluyéndose de la batalla y, Lewis Hamilton, quien podría haber mantenido un poco más de tiempo la batalla viva, carrera tras carrera termina con sus opciones al que sería su 8º Título de F1, terminando, esta vez, 6º, por detrás de Kimi Antonelli.

articles.title: Sun Goddess passes 'massive test' to rule supreme in Cheveley Park
articles.summary: Aidan O'Brien's star filly Sun Goddess recorded a third Group One success with an emphatic display in the Cheveley Park Stakes, in a record-setting time.
articles.body:
Sun Goddess and fellow Group One heroine Senorita Bonita travelled in tandem in midfield as Snowing and Moonrise set a strong pace up the six furlongs of the Rowley Mile.

Senorita Bonita was the first to show her hand, with the smooth-travelling Libertango launching her attack under Billy Loughnane on the far side from the back of the field.

But Sun Goddess found plenty for Ryan Moore on meeting the rising ground, with the 5-6 favourite engaging top gear to win by a going-away length from Libertango, making it her third top-level win of the campaign. Senorita Bonita was only able to finish fifth after not getting home.

O'Brien, who saddled this year's 1000 Guineas heroine True Love to win this race 12 months ago, said: "That is a massive run after winning over seven furlongs (Moyglare Stud Stakes) on soft ground, it was some change today. It was a massive test and she's passed it.

"She looks a freak doesn't she to be doing what she is doing and you have to remember she's a two-year-old filly racing at the top level every day. It's incredible and I can't remember having one that classy, with that speed and distance range before, she looks really unusual.

"She's unique and to have the mental capacity and physical (attributes) to match it. She's come back there and she's in no way stressed at all.

"She came off the bridle early which meant she would get into her tempo as we were worried she would travel and then come off the bridle and find everything happening too quickly. But once she came off it early she was always going to be really hard to handle.

"She's big and doesn't look like a two-year-old, she's more like a three-year-old and a massive big specimen. Even if she didn't change any from now until next year she would be plenty big and would still be considered a big three-year-old. It's very unusual."

He went on: "The lads got her in Doncaster and it was great she was able to go back and win that (sales) race at York earlier in the summer, it's a great initiative and a very big pot."

Sun Goddess was made 6-4 favourite for next year's 1000 Guineas by BOYLE Sports, but before that she could board the plane to Keeneland for the Breeders' Cup to test her mettle over a mile.

O'Brien added: "We'll see how she is and the next week or so will tell us how she is and whether this has taken much out of her.

"She is not blowing very hard and when we were tacking up there was no anxiety. She's as cool as a cucumber and Ryan was over the moon with her."

images.caption: Image: Ryan Moore on Sun Goddess wins the Tattersalls Sceptre Sessions Cheveley Park Stakes

articles.title: Orthodox leaves Prix Morny defeat behind in Middle Park
articles.summary: The Clive Cox-trained Norfolk hero Orthodox bounced back from his Prix Morny defeat with a gutsy display to see off Force Noir in a thrilling finish to the Middle Park at Newmarket.
articles.body:
Force Noir cut out the early running as he set a sharp pace at the head of field, but Rossa Ryan put down his challenge early and asked Norfolk Stakes winner Orthodox for an effort at the three-furlong marker.

The Clive Cox-trained 7-2 chance was pushed all the way to the line by Robson De Aguiar's Force Noir at a big price and just prevailed by a neck, with favourite Inner City Blues never getting into it.

It was a welcome return to winning ways for the Royal Ascot scorer and Cox said: "We always had confidence in him and it was always a question of would he handle the track with the quicker ground a bonus for this time of year.

"Sometimes it is not as quick as this and I'm just thrilled he has shown what we all see at home, as he is pretty special in the mornings and he's special in the afternoons as well. He's tough and very able and it was a big team effort to get him here and I'm over the moon.

"I think he got away with the track and Rossa was supreme the way he coaxed him through the dip and then set sail after that. I thought it was a supreme ride and I'm thrilled. Rossa is a regular in the mornings and knows exactly what he's riding and what he's up against as well."

It was the third time Cox has scooped the Middle Park after Reckless Abandon (2012) and Supremacy (2020) who like Orthodox was owned by Jason Goddard.

With his future clearly lying in the sprint division in which Cox regularly thrives, Orthodox was handed a quote of 12-1 by Ladbrokes and Coral for next year's Commonwealth Cup at the Royal meeting.

However, before that a trip to America for the Breeders' Cup will be discussed by connections.

Cox continued: "I would be hugely excited by this fellow. I know his family really well and his aunt won the Queen Mary for us (Heartache).

"I think he's blessed with the ability to race over five furlongs or six, but I don't think there can be any doubt he gets six and he proved that today.

"He had the gears to win well over five furlongs at Ascot and he's a very talented sprinter and a joy to have.

"It's a joy to have these horses and it means the world. He could go to the Breeders' Cup and we'll see how he comes back and discuss it with Jason. It is a possibility, but we have to enjoy today first and then discuss the future over the next few days."

Haffner records straightforward Royal Lodge success

Haffner left a disappointing performance in the National Stakes firmly behind him with a clear-cut victory in the Tattersalls Online Royal Lodge Stakes at Newmarket.

The Charlie Appleby-trained pair of Quest For Stars and First Law disputed the early lead with the latter racing keenly on the far side of the course in isolation with Iwasjustsaying.

The Aidan O'Brien-trained Haffner was the first to lay down his challenge a furlong and a half out and pulled clear of the field with First Law and Quest For Stars unable to go with him.

The well-backed 7-4 favourite went on to oblige by one and a quarter lengths to give O'Brien a record eighth Royal Lodge and Ryan Moore his first. Karl Burke's Burning Up stayed on best of the rest for second in the colours of last year's winner, Bow Echo.

O'Brien said: "The ground got soft at the Curragh the last day which didn't suit him. He's going to be a lovely middle-distance horse next year, he's going to be a French Derby type horse. He'll get the Guineas trip on his ear, will stay a mile and a quarter and could even get further, so I'm delighted.

"He's a good mover and we didn't think the ground was going to be as soft as it was at the Curragh. He's a beautiful mover and we were happy to draw a line through that and he was always in control today. Ryan gave him a beautiful uncomplicated ride and it was very simple really.

"His form was different class really and his only blip was in the National Stakes. We knew that was because of the ground and we knew he would get the mile very easily. He's an Acomb winner and his form is so strong."

Paddy Power make Haffner a 4-1 chance for the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf at Keeneland next month and O'Brien indicated that could be the next destination for the talented son of Justify.

O'Brien added: "America is very possible next, where he will get nice ground. He would love the Breeders' Cup round a bend and the mile would be very easy for him, so we'll see what the lads want to do.

"America was always a possibility and the last day was a blip, but we had to come here today to make sure we knew exactly that it was and he's got back on track.

"I think he could start in a Guineas next year and then we will see him stepping up in trip."

articles.title: Lando Norris: McLaren driver calls for Franco Colapinto race ban after Azerbaijan GP three-car collision with Alpines
articles.summary: Franco Colapinto apologetic for the "big mistake" that saw him cause chain reaction collision with team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris, forcing all three to retire; Colapinto to serve grid drop at Bahrain GP; Norris says "just some drivers that shouldn't be in Formula 1"
articles.body:
At the first Safety Car restart on lap 36, Colapinto badly misjudged his braking into the first corner and, carrying too much speed, steamed into the side of Alpine team-mate Gasly, whose car was sent into Norris' McLaren on its outside.

Norris was spun into the barriers, with the two Alpines also forced to retire with damage. Gasly had been running seventh, Norris eighth and Colapinto 10th.

A frustrated Norris said: "At the end of the day, I just got taken out.

"Just some drivers that shouldn't be in Formula 1, to be honest."

Speaking to the written media, the reigning world champion added: "I've not seen it, but if you cause a crash in a restart like this, you should have at least a one-race ban.

"I just got taken out. And the FIA should be stricter by starting to hand out bans for this kind of stuff."

Colapinto was apologetic on both team radio and then in his interviews afterwards for what he admitted was a "big mistake".

"Just to all the team, not only to Pierre, but it's just a big mistake," said Colapinto.

"So a big, big sorry to Pierre, to everyone in the factory that has been working really hard. We were with both cars in the points so very sad and disappointed.

"Big, big sorry, it's a big mistake. Just cold brakes, cold tyres and locked up and completely out of control.

"Unfortunately, I also took Pierre out and Lando of course but big sorry to both of them."

Colapinto was handed a 10-second time penalty by stewards for causing the collision but, as he had already retired from the race and so could not serve it, the sanction was converted into a five-place grid penalty for this coming week's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

F1 has a totting-up procedure in place for indiscretions on track, with drivers banned for a race if they accrue 12 penalty points on their superlicence over a rolling 12-month period. Colapinto, who is currently on four points, did not have any penalty points applied to his licence for Saturday's incident in addition to the in-lieu Bahrain grid drop.

'You want to be against the best drivers - Norris unimpressed with Colapinto error

Norris described Colapinto's driving as "just careless" and unbecoming of F1.

"It costs a lot of money, all my parts are in the bin now," he added.

"It is not driving that deserves to be in Formula 1

"In Formula 1 you would expect that drivers can anticipate that the grip will be low and tyre temperatures are low.

"You want to be against the best drivers and when stuff like this happens it is because, yeah, they shouldn't be there."

Norris said he had already been enduring an "impossible race" owing to straight-line speed issues with his car. He had dropped behind Gasly six laps earlier by running wide at the first turn.

I'm still struggling to process the outcome - Gasly's reaction to costly Alpine result

Gasly had been on course to equal his second-best result of the season with seventh place amid a strong weekend on the street track for the Frenchman.

With Colapinto also having been running in the points at the time of the Safety Car, Alpine were on course to almost wipe out their pre-race deficit of nine points to rivals Racing Bulls - who at that stage ran 12th and 14th - in the chase for fifth place in the Constructors' Championship.

However, they leave the race 15 points behind Racing Bulls after a late-race surge saw Arvid Lindblad take seventh place instead.

Admitting he was almost lost for words, Gasly told Sky Sports F1 : "It's not easy.

"We did a very good weekend and it was one of the best race cars we've had this season and the pace was great, keeping up with Lewis [Hamilton] and Lando for most of the race and we had a 14 or 15-second gap to the midfield.

"So I think a lot of positives to take away but I'm still struggling to process the outcome and the fact we had both cars in the points and in the end we got outscored by Racing Bulls by a lot of points.

"Not an ideal day but I'm sure we are going to move on from it. Unfortunately, we have lost out today, hopefully we can make it up to the end of the year."

Gasly spoke on Wednesday about the "completely inappropriate" social media abuse that he and family members had received in the wake of an incident on track with Colapinto at the previous race in Madrid. Colapinto and Alpine have consistently condemned abuse aimed at other drivers from some Argentine fans online.

Colapinto and Gasly are both already confirmed at the team for next season.

Asked if he was confident his partnership with Colapinto could continue to work, Gasly replied: "Respect. It's all about respect. As long as there is respect, everything is possible."

Colapinto added: "We are good. We have always been quite good together. Since we worked together for the first time, we got on very well so we need to move on."

articles.title: Pierre Royal strikes Cambridgeshire gold for Ireland
articles.summary: A first trip to Newmarket was a winning one for Adrian McGuinness as the only Irish raider Pierre Royal struck gold in the coveted Cambridgeshire Handicap.
articles.body:
But connections of the Adrian McGuinness-trained four-year-old had a tense wait before the judge confirmed he had edged Crest Of Fire to become the first Irish-trained winner of the race this century.

Both the winner and second came from the group on the far side and it was Jack Channon's Crest Of Fire who was first to emerge in the hands of Tom Marquand.

But he was stalked all the way by the Mikey Sheehy-ridden Pierre Royal and the 33-1 shot reeled him to just get up.

Altareq ran a huge race for Jim Goldie and Lauren Young to claim third at 100-1 with favourite Gavriel the best of the near-side runners in fourth.

McGuinness said: "I wasn't surprised as we have been running him on soft ground and it's been killing me. He was third in an Irish Cambridgeshire on soft ground and I said I'd come here for the better ground. We gave it some cheer and I've just dashed back from the winning post.

"We only made our minds up to come last Monday and he ran very well in the Irish Cambridgeshire and then we ran him back over one-mile-two and it was soft and he didn't handle it.

"He's a lovely horse to train and he's very easy on himself, he travels over well and he eats and like myself can get a bit big sometimes. He just eats, sleeps and drinks.

"There's a great bunch of lads involved in this horse and they've had a great time with him. He's paid his way plenty and cost only 48,000 guineas at Newmarket last year."

He went on: "I told Mikey to sit out the back as he had plenty of boot and in all fairness to Mikey I think one of his last rides for me he took was a spare on a reserve that won the Galway Mile and he's a top-class rider.

"I'm delighted I got him and only rang his agent a couple of days ago to see if he was available as I wanted to pick someone who is lucky for me. He's top notch."

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli: F1 championship leader says he was 'driving like his grandma' due to lack of confidence at Azerbaijan GP
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli's world champions lead over George Russell was reduced to 66 points following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix; Antonelli recovered from 16th on the grid to finish fifth, while Russel won from pole position
articles.body:
Antonelli staged a decent recovery in Saturday's race to come from 16th on the grid, following a crash in qualifying, to finish fifth, but his championship lead over his Mercedes team-mate George Russell was reduced to 66 points as the Brit claimed victory.

The 20-year-old Italian has shown remarkable consistency to build a commanding lead at the top of the standings, but struggled in Baku after missing a significant chunk of practice due to technical issues with his car.

"I was driving a bit like my grandmother today, just damage save mode," Antonelli said. "I didn't take risks. Before making a move, I was making sure that I could go for it."

Expectations were high given Antonelli had remarkably come from 19th on the grid to win his home race at Monza earlier in September, but his progress was far more steady this time around.

"If I had the same pace as at Monza or in previous races, it would have been different," Antonelli said.

"It would have been like just full attack. But today, I realised very early that first of all, it was a lot harder to overtake with a train of cars all in Overtake Mode, then I didn't have the same pace as I had previously, so the mindset changed very quickly."

Antonelli actually dropped a place at the start, and it took him 17 laps to work his way up into the top 10.

He then benefitted from errors made by drivers ahead as he made further progress. He also survived a near-miss at the first of two rolling restarts following Safety Cars as he avoided a crash that took three cars out of the race, and was able to continue despite contact with the Haas of Oliver Bearman.

Antonelli said: "After the restart, I had big floor damage. My whole left side was gone with the contact.

"After that, the car was very sketchy to drive, and I still tried to get to P4, but all in all, it's one of those days where you have to be happy with P5.

"Also seeing so many people doing mistakes, you kind of pull back a little bit because I just took advantage of everyone else's mistakes and just move forward."

Antonelli doesn't have to wait long to return to the track with the second of a triple-header of races coming next weekend with the Bahrain Grand Prix, which is being hosted by Malaysia amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

Russell produced his most complete weekend since the opening round of the season in Australia, taking a victory that would have been dominant without the Safety Car interruptions.

Antonelli remains a heavy favourite for the title, especially given Russell must take a grid penalty for changing his engine between now and the end of the season.

It was therefore unsurprising that the championship leader was retaining a positive outlook ahead of the next race.

"It's exciting," Antonelli told Sky Sports F1 . "George has done an incredible weekend, he's driven incredibly. He had a lot of confidence.

"And this weekend was my worst of the year by far in terms of performance. I wasn't there, I wasn't really present, especially with what happened so early on."

articles.title: Azerbaijan Grand Prix: Harry Benjamin's driver ratings as George Russell wins in Baku
articles.summary: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin rates how the drivers performed during the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
articles.body:
George Russell led from start to finish as he dominated the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The victory reduced the championship lead of his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to 66 points - from 81 - after the Italian finished fifth, although he had recovered from starting 16th on the grid.

Max Verstappen pushed Russell for the win as he took second place, less than two tenths of a second behind. Fellow Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar completed the podium by finishing third on his return to racing following a wrist injury.

Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Baku.

Pretty difficult to find fault with this one. Fastest on Thursday, produced a stunning qualifying lap to take pole by more than eight tenths and controlled the race before holding off Max Verstappen under huge pressure at the end.

His eighth place in qualifying looked poor on paper but came with genuine power and energy deployment problems. Charged through the field on Saturday, passed Oscar Piastri for second and pushed Russell all the way to the line. An excellent recovery.

What a way to return after three races on the sidelines. Out-qualified Verstappen with fourth on the grid, showed excellent pace early in the race and finished on the podium while also playing the team game when Verstappen came through.

Second on the grid was an excellent qualifying result, although a tow certainly helped him get there. Ferrari simply didn't have the race pace to stay with Russell and the Red Bulls and fourth felt about the maximum available by the end.

A weekend of two very different halves. Crashing out in Q1 was a costly and unnecessary mistake, but he responded with a patient recovery from 16th to fifth despite picking up floor damage during the race.

His qualifying result was hurt by Ferrari's run plan leaving him without the tow he needed, but sixth in both qualifying and the race still made for a fairly quiet weekend. Solid enough, although Leclerc had the upper hand when it mattered.

Recovered again impressively after crashing in practice and starting 15th. Took advantage of the chaos when it came and then stole seventh from Esteban Ocon by the tiniest of margins at the finish. Goes a long way to limiting the grief he might get from punting into his Racing Bulls team-mate at Turn One.

A really strong race from the Haas driver after starting outside the top 10. Made some decisive moves as others fell into trouble and briefly looked set for seventh before Lindblad pinched it on the line.

Good enough to narrowly miss Q3 and stayed in the points despite losing out to Ocon during the race. Contact with Antonelli at the first restart was a slightly messy moment in an otherwise useful result for Haas.

The pace was encouraging and ninth in qualifying would have been Williams' best grid position of the season but failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags earned him a five-place grid penalty. Recovered from as low as 19th in the race to grab the final point.

Russell wins despite late Verstappen challenge

Norris says Colapinto should be banned after accident

Audi's big upgrade didn't translate into qualifying. However, Hulk recovered reasonably well to 11th thanks to the carnage ahead but lost the final point to Sainz late on.

Back at Racing Bulls after three races with Red Bull and showed reasonable pace to qualify 12th before penalties moved him up the grid. His race was badly affected when team-mate Lindblad made contact with him in the chaotic second restart, leaving 12th a difficult result to judge too harshly.

For most of the weekend this was heading towards a very high score for the McLaren driver. Third in qualifying and running in the podium positions for much of the race. But his big lock-up at Turn One dropped him all the way down the order and threw away a potentially excellent result.

Looked rapid compared with Cadillac team-mate Valtteri Bottas in the early part of the weekend. But a suspected Q2 challenge didn't quite materialise.

Another difficult weekend for Audi despite all the new parts on the car. Out in Q1 alongside Hulkenberg and although he made progress on race day, it was not the return he would have hoped for.

His final qualifying lap was deleted for being set under double-waved yellow flags, leaving him at the back of the order. Almost made it to the finish but found the barriers late on.

The weekend had actually been going well after reaching Q3 and starting ninth. But his enormous lock-up at the second restart wiped out team-mate Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris as well as his own race, turning a potential double points finish for Alpine into nothing.

A really good weekend that deserved so much better. Qualified seventh and was still running there at the final restart before being taken out by his team-mate through no fault of his own.

Not the cleanest weekend for McLaren's world champion. A mistake on his final qualifying lap left him fifth and another lock-up during the race had already cost him places before he became an innocent victim of Colapinto's restart crash.

Was behind Sainz in qualifying before his team-mate's penalty shuffled the grid. His race ended with an error into the barriers at Turn Four which brought out the first safety car, so a difficult weekend despite signs of improvement from the car.

Another weekend where there wasn't much opportunity to show anything. Qualified 19th, took a back-of-grid power-unit penalty and then retired with a mechanical problem in a miserable race for Aston Martin.

Qualified behind Alonso before also taking his own penalty. Another mechanical retirement meant Aston Martin left Baku without either car reaching the finish.

articles.title: Azerbaijan Grand Prix: George Russell 'comes through other side' after 'real tough period'
articles.summary: George Russell described the Azerbaijan Grand Prix as "the most dominant weekend I've had in my career" after a win that felt like vindication.
articles.body:
For George Russell, this one felt like vindication, proof that he had "come through the other side" and was back to his best after what he acknowledged was a "real tough period" during this Formula 1 season.

The Mercedes driver's victory in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, holding off Red Bull's Max Verstappen in one of the closest finishes in history, was his first since the end of June - seven races ago.

In that time, team-mate Kimi Antonelli has won three times, to take his tally of victories to eight for the season.

So Russell needed this, his third victory, in a year that he started as championship favourite. Instead, Antonelli has taken the season by the throat and all but crushed the life out of Russell's hopes.

Now, though, a glimmer of hope still exists for Russell, even if he is too realistic to think too much about it for now.

His win, combined with Antonelli's fifth place after what the Italian admitted was his "worst weekend of the year in terms of performance", has cut the points gap between them to 66.

That's still huge, with either seven or eight races still to go, and 25 points for a win. But it's a lot better than the 81-point margin Russell faced before Baku.

"My team-mate's had an incredible season," Russell said. "He's been pretty flawless throughout, but now we're getting to crunch time.

"But I'm just going to focus on myself. You know, if I continue delivering performances like I've done this weekend, no matter what happens towards the end of the season, I'll be happy."

With the grand prix brought forward 24 hours from the usual Sunday slot, it was an appropriate result for a man whose prowess in qualifying has earned him the nickname 'Mr Saturday'.

Russell wins despite late Verstappen challenge

Russell faultless and Hadjar excellent on return - driver ratings

Russell has been through the mill in 2026. He dominated the intra-team battle last year, but the tables have turned dramatically this season, as Antonelli felt immediately at home in the new Mercedes after the biggest rule changes in F1 history, and the Briton very much did not.

For Russell, the blows have kept coming. Every apparent revival was met with another setback. Every time he felt he had made progress, Antonelli's apparently effortless way of extracting that little bit more from the car chastened him.

No experience was more painful than the Italian Grand Prix at Monza two races ago, when Russell started from the front row, and Antonelli 19th after a grid penalty.

Russell knew it was a golden opportunity to make up ground. Instead, it was Antonelli who won the race, with what will go down as one of the greatest drives in history. Russell looked on the verge of tears after that one.

But he kept the belief, and in Baku it all came together.

Russell was a man on a mission all weekend, fastest from the moment he took to the track, while Antonelli, after losing half the two hours of practice on the first day, lost his cool.

He made a mistake in qualifying, took a wheel off on an inside wall, and started 16th. There was to be no repeat of Monza, even if fifth was a very creditable comeback result.

"I felt always a step behind," Antonelli said, "and especially with the mistake in qualifying the confidence level was not high and today was about damage limitation.

"Just probably also the mindset was not in the best place. I wasn't there. I wasn't really present, especially with what happened so early on and just didn't take the same risks, especially after qualifying.

"Today was more damage-safe mode instead of full attack. I just make sure next weekend we get back in the right level."

If he does, this will go down as a blip in an otherwise stunningly impressive breakthrough season by a potential future great. But the parallels with last year are unavoidable.

In 2025, McLaren's Oscar Piastri arrived in Azerbaijan apparently in control of the championship, and possessing a big lead over team-mate Lando Norris, albeit less than half what Antonelli's is now.

But Piastri had some kind of meltdown on the streets of Baku, what he described after arriving back in the city this week as "the worst race of my career".

And after that, the wheels came off for the Australian, and he was overtaken by the end of the year not only by Norris, but also by Verstappen.

There is no reason to believe Antonelli will suffer the same fate. But he still has something to process in the few days before taking to the track again in Malaysia on Friday.

This was the first time Russell has produced a weekend like this all year, when he was simply superior. Before, even when he won, Antonelli was right there with him, sometimes even faster.

How did Russell do this? It has taken hard work and analysis on his part and with his engineers.

He hasn't been comfortable in this year's car, feeling it does not suit his driving style, so he has had to put in the effort to make the driving feel natural. And he feels he is finally getting somewhere.

Deputy team principal Bradley Lord said: "He had some difficult moments before the summer break, some soul-searching as well at points, and he's come back really strong, focused on the driving, focusing on the essentials of what he needs to do to put his weekends together step by step."

Russell said: "I'm very proud of the resilience that I and my close group of engineers have shown during the tough periods this year because there's been a lot of hard work to overcome some of the challenges, to adapt my driving style to suit this new car better.

"And F1 is so tough, you don't get opportunities to practise this, and finally it's coming to me a bit more intuitively than it once did, and I'm gaining confidence. And especially on circuits like this, it just allows you to eke out that little bit more on the brakes, get that little bit closer to the walls, and it's been a flawless weekend.

"It's been four races since the (summer) break. I've been on the front row in three of them, three podiums from the four races. I feel I can fight for victory week in, week out now."

Norris says Colapinto should be banned after accident

Azerbaijan GP Review: Vettel Gives His Verdict

The win was looking comfortable for a while, as he romped away at the front in the first stint while Piastri delayed Verstappen.

But two mid-race safety cars closed up the field and left Verstappen right on Russell's tail.

Russell could not shake him off, but he continued to be flawless. Even when slowing for a yellow flag on the final lap caused a loss of turbo boost pressure and left him vulnerable on the run to the flag.

"It's for sure the most dominant weekend I've had in my career," Russell said. "So that has come at a really great moment. And also to achieve it on a circuit that requires so much commitment and confidence, I'm really proud of, because it would have been very easy for me to lose the faith this season."

Mercedes have lost their early season dominance over the summer, but the Bahrain/Malaysia race will see their first big upgrade for a while.

"I'm really excited," Russell said. "That's going to be a good step forward.

"Our car has been working exceptionally well on the low-drag circuits. We've got a really efficient car, so here at Baku we've been exceptionally fast. But I think from next week onwards, we're hoping to make a bigger step to the rest of the field. But nothing's sure until we see how it pans out in reality."

And even if Antonelli cannot be anything but still a strong favourite, the same goes for the championship.

"There's much less pressure on me than there is on him," Russell said. "Yesterday was probably his first mistake of this whole season in a proper session, qualifying, race, and he still came home in P5 today.

"I didn't really consider myself in this fight for a number of races, purely because my performance wasn't strong enough.

"Now I feel like if the season were to have started today, or since the summer break, you know, I feel very much I would have been able to fight.

"Now I've got this big deficit. It can change quick. So I'm not chasing that. I'm chasing to win every race, and what will be, will be."

articles.standfirst: Malaysia acoge el Gran Premio de Bahrein tras su cancelación por la Guerra en Oriente Medio
articles.summary: Malaysia acoge el Gran Premio de Bahrein tras su cancelación por la Guerra en Oriente Medio
articles.body: El Mundial de F1 regresa a Malasia casi 10 años después, aunque de una forma que no les hubiera gustado. Tras el estallido de la Guerra en Oriente Medio a principios de año, el Mundial de F1 se vio trastocado al tener que cancelar Bahrein y Arabia Saudí, a la espera aún de lo que suceda con Qatar y Abu Dhabi. Sin embargo, el Sepang International Circuit se ha postulado como un sustituto y acogerá el Gran Premio de Bahrein este fin de semana, regresando así tras su última aparición en 2017, cuya carrera ganó Max Verstappen. Kimi Antonelli sigue líder del Mundial a pesar de las dificultades en Bakú. El piloto italiano cometió un error en Q1 que le condenó la carrera, acabando 5º y consiguiendo tan sólo 10 puntos. Mientras, su compañero de equipo, y principal rival por el Título, George Russell, le pegó un pequeño bocado en la general de 15 puntos tras ganar por una décima a Max Verstappen en el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán. Se encuentra por lo tanto a 66 puntos de diferencia y, aunque sean varios, aún queda mucho por jugar. Los problemas se le acumulan a Aston Martin y, en especial, a Honda, acabando con la paciencia del piloto español. El Bicampeón del Mundo tan solo completó 21 vueltas muy frustrantes y en las que se le vio claramente enfadado, ante la incapacidad hacerle frente a los rivales con su monoplaza. Además, a esto se le añade el desastre que ha supuesto el fin de semana en general. Partía con una sanción de 25 posiciones por cambiar su Unidad de Potencia, la cual se acabó rompiendo, haciendo que tuvieran que volver a montar el motor antiguo. Problemas que se suman y que van calando en el piloto español, cuya amenaza de acabar su historia con la Fórmula 1 cada vez se hace más latente. Con mejoras en su Williams, aunque tampoco como para lanzar cohetes, Carlos ha podido sacarle provecho y, tras meterse en Q3 y clasificar 9º, el madrileño tuvo que volver a tirar de talento para salvar un punto. Una sanción por bandera amarilla condenó a Carlos Sainz a salir desde la 14ª posición, la cuál acabó siendo un desastre. Perdió varias posiciones en la salida y no tuvo más remedio que remontar, aprovechándose, eso sí, de los diversos incidentes que se formaron por delante. Finalmente pudo pasar a Hulkenberg a menos de 5 vueltas para el final, firmando así un 10º puesto. Como es habitual, el Gran Premio de Bahrein de Fórmula 1 2026 se podrá ver en directo por televisión a través de DAZN F1 y en Movistar +. También tienes la opción de seguir todo lo que suceda en la carrera en el circuito de Sepang a través de los directos de MARCA.com y la transmisión de la carrera en Radio MARCA. articles.title: Detained Tunisian flotilla activists: Worsening health amid family anguish
articles.summary: As activists’ health deteriorates, families describe the toll of separation, hunger strikes and uncertainty.
articles.body:
Tunis, Tunisia – For nine-year-old Yassar Naouar, visiting his father in prison has become an exercise in staying strong. He tries not to cry in front of Wael , fearing that seeing his son in tears would make an already painful situation harder for him. After leaving the prison, Yassar finds a corner where he can finally let the tears fall.

Hichem Naouar, Yassar’s grandfather, says the boy has changed since his father was detained . He now sleeps beside his mother after waking up screaming at night and his results at school have worsened. When Yassar told his mother that other children kept asking whether his father was a thief, she asked him what he thought.

Wael’s youngest child, four-year-old Sumud, is too young to understand why her father is in prison. Hichem says he took her to visit him. When she saw her father behind the glass, she leaned forward to embrace him, only to hit her head against the barrier.

Hichem spoke to Al Jazeera on Wednesday outside the Tunis Court of Appeal, where he had gone to follow the latest challenge to Wael’s detention . He repeatedly choked up as he described what he had seen during his most recent visit.

Wael was sitting with his hand against his cheek, his father said, his elbow trembling and his gaze fixed in the distance. He was struggling to see clearly and to keep water down without vomiting. He was dizzy and had difficulty controlling his left leg. Wael later told Hichem that other prisoners had said he sometimes wakes during the night calling out his youngest daughter’s name.

For his father, however, Wael’s story is also about the kind of person he has been. He recalled an incident during the Sumud land convoy in Libya in May, when armed men tried to kidnap another participant. Wael intervened, pulled the man away and helped him escape before returning to the men and telling them they could take him instead.

During the first Sumud flotilla , a woman fell into the sea and was close to drowning. Wael immediately jumped in and rescued her.

“Wael’s strength is in the strength of his ideas and in his commitment to his people. Whenever he heard about any injustice against workers or employees, you would always find him at the forefront,” Hichem said.

Wael, 41, began a hunger strike on August 16 to protest his continued detention and was transferred to hospital as his condition deteriorated. He suspended his strike after 38 days following appeals from his lawyers and supporters, saying the decision did not mean abandoning his demands.

Four activists, Ghassan Henchiri, Ghassan Boughdiri and Nabil Channoufi, have been held since March following an investigation by Tunisia’s Economic and Financial Judicial Pole, a specialised body that handles financial and economic crimes. The investigation concerns alleged financial irregularities linked to fundraising for the Global Sumud Flotilla, an international campaign seeking to deliver aid to Gaza and challenge Israel’s blockade of the Palestinian territory.

The state-owned TAP news agency, citing judicial sources, reported that investigators are examining the origin and use of funds collected for the flotilla and whether any were diverted for other purposes. The activists and their defence team have repeatedly denied wrongdoing and maintain their innocence. None of the four has been convicted.

For their lawyers, the issue is also why the men should remain in prison while the investigation continues.

Ghassan Ghribi, a member of the defence committee, described the latest extension of their pretrial detention as an “exception to the exception”, arguing that freedom should be the rule and detention the exception. The four-month extension was ordered on September 11 and the defence challenged the decision before the Court of Appeal in Tunis.

“The investigating judge spent six months on the case without carrying out any investigative work, other than questioning the activists,” Ghribi told Al Jazeera. He said the extension should be based on clear reasons and that the four men were being made to pay the price for what he described as a lack of investigative work.

The Court of Appeal rejected the challenge on Wednesday, leaving the quartet in pretrial detention for another four months while the investigation continues. Henchiri, Boughdiri and Channoufi remain on hunger strike.

Authorities have presented the case as a financial investigation into the handling of funds raised for the flotilla, rather than a prosecution linked to the men’s political or pro-Palestinian activities. The government has rejected accusations that the judiciary is being used to silence opponents, saying the judiciary is independent and that legal proceedings are conducted according to the law.

The fallout has also widened beyond the four men. Fourteen people detained after the September 19 protest calling for their release have since been placed in pretrial detention, lawyer Rafed Rabbeh confirmed to Al Jazeera on Friday. Among them is a 17-year-old who was brought before a juvenile judge. Tunisia’s Child Protection Code says priority should be given to preventive and educational measures and that pretrial detention should be avoided as much as possible for children.

Rabbeh said the detainees face several charges, including participating in a gathering allegedly intended to disturb public order and commit an offence, publicly attributing unlawful acts to a public official without proof, and making public statements deemed to damage the reputation of a person or official body. The charges are based on several provisions of Tunisia’s Penal Code.

Speaking by phone from Gafsa, Ghassan Henchiri’s father, Sebti, said his son remains conscious but is visibly exhausted after being on hunger strike since September 9.

“According to what his sister told me after visiting him, he is still holding up. The fatigue is visible. He is exhausted, but he is still conscious,” Sebti said.

Ghassan has not been taken outside the prison for further medical examination of a head injury sustained during his detention in Israel, Sebti told Al Jazeera. Ghassan and his family have raised the issue with both the prison administration and investigating judge. They were promised that he would receive the necessary medical examinations, but that has not happened, Sebti said.

“It could be a superficial injury, but with the conditions in prison and the high temperatures, it has exhausted him,” he said.

Ghassan also has other health problems, including living with one kidney and suffering from back problems, Sebti said. He has developed a skin rash that keeps him from sleeping, but his request to see a dermatologist was rejected because the prison doctor did not consider it serious, Sebti said.

“I will remain steadfast, I will not give up my right and these malicious accusations are false,” Ghassan told his father.

“He is my son, my brother, my companion, my whole life,” Sebti said. “Ghassan is a man of integrity. I am not saying that because I am his father. Everyone knows that about him.”

Ghassan’s detention has also reshaped family life. He had been working at a high school and was recently engaged, Sebti said.

He described Ghassan’s political commitment as something rooted in the family. He has been involved in student activism and later trade unions since 1978, campaigning for freedom, the right to organise and a better, more dignified life for Tunisians. Ghassan grew up with those principles and was influenced by his father’s activism.

“This is what Ghassan was raised on and what influenced him,” Sebti said.

Human Rights Watch has also raised concerns over the use of financial and money-laundering investigations against civil society actors in Tunisia.

For the Naouar and Henchiri families, the impact of the detentions is being felt at home, in prison visits, anxious phone calls and children asking when their fathers will return.

Yassar still asks about his father and has told his grandfather he is ready to go on hunger strike too.

Asked where her father is, four-year-old Sumud answers: “Palestine. Prison”.

articles.title: El Mundial de F1 es... ¿cosa de dos?
articles.standfirst: George Russell gana en Azerbaiyán y se coloca a 66 de Antonelli con ocho carreras para la conclusión del campeonato
articles.summary: George Russell gana en Azerbaiyán y se coloca a 66 de Antonelli con ocho carreras para la conclusión del campeonato
articles.body: "Tengo mucha menos presión que él. Su año es perfecto y cometió su primer error en la clasificación. Igualmente, vuelve a casa con un quinto puesto. Tengo un gran déficit, puede cambiar... pero no busco eso. Sólo quiero ganar cada carrera y que lo que sea, será", explicaba un radiante George Russell tras un Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán perfecto. El de la octava victoria de su vida, el primer Grand Chelem (pole, victoria, vuelta rápida y todas las vueltas lideradas) de su vida. Y el del mensaje a un Kimi Antonelli que si bien tiene 66 puntos de renta, ahora vuelve el mejor Russell. Evidentemente, la fuerza de Antonelli es superior y sigue sin fallar... o compensa sus pocos errores con madurez. En la clasificación no valoró del todo bien los riesgos y reventó su Mercedes, pero en carrera pudo remontar con cabeza hasta el quinto. Mantiene diferencia a favor y cambiará el tipo de circuito para seguir atacando. "El único foco era maximizar los puntos, no cometer riesgos y tener paciencia para adelantar", explicaba el italiano. Con un Mundial en la mano y ahora parece cosa de dos. Porque Hamilton está casi descartado tras caer a más de 100 puntos de desventaja tras otro Gran Premio aciago. Y Norris, que venía con fuerza en circuitos revirados, cayó con un cero tras el fallo de Colapinto. El Mundial está entre Antonelli y un Russell que ha vuelto a sonreír y rozar la perfección. Desde Australia y el sprint de China, no aparecía su versión más demoledora. Una en la que entiende qué le pide el monoplaza y puede extraer al máximo que haga sombra al brillante talento de su compañero de equipo. Además, hay un argumento más a favor de su mano a mano, las mejoras que vendrán en Malasia. "Estoy emocionado, llegan pronto. Será un paso más. Tenemos un coche que funciona muy bien en circuitos de baja carga, es muy eficiente. Aquí y en Monza iba muy bien, pero necesitábamos dar un paso más para los próximos en comparación al resto de la parrilla", apuntó Russell. Mercedes seguirá creciendo y quizá vuelva esa pelea que sólo se vio en carreras como Barcelona o Canadá y desapareció en el verano. De cualquier forma, la baraja ganadora sigue al otro lado del box. Aunque la presión regresa, que es un elemento que no había aparecido en toda la temporada. Antonelli sigue al mando, pero su Mundial tiene un competidor serio en el piloto que parecía opacado y condenado a ser el segundo plato... del título de la joya.

articles.title: ¡Briatore quiere castigar a Colapinto tras su gran error!
articles.standfirst: El italiano podría tomar una decisión drástica con el argentino... y la prensa inglesa lo relaciona con una carrera de suspensión
articles.summary: El italiano podría tomar una decisión drástica con el argentino... y la prensa inglesa lo relaciona con una carrera de suspensión
articles.body: Al margen de la victoria de George Russell, la gran imagen del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán fue de Franco Colapinto. El argentino preparó un momento dramático en la primera resalida de la carrera, al pasarse de frenada en la recta y formar una montonera que acabó con la carrera de su compañero de equipo, Pierre Gasly, y de Lando Norris. Tenía puntos, tuvo que abandonar y el campeón del 2025 arremetió contra el piloto de Alpine con una afirmación tajante: "Hay pilotos que no deberían estar en la Fórmula 1". Colapinto cometió un error grave, mucho más que su salida a la grava cuando peleaba por los puestos del podio en las Lesmos de Monza. Por una relanzada quizá precipitada y con exceso de optimismo para ganar posiciones de cabeza. "Bloqueé cuando empecé a frenar y perdí totalmente el control en la frenada", relató. Con un mensaje en el que sus disculpas eran totales. "Pido perdón al equipo, a la fábrica... y a Pierre [Gasly]", expresó. Allí está el principal lío. Colapinto dejó a su equipo en cero puntos, algo más delicado si cabe si el jefe del negocio es un Flavio Briatore tajante y directo para señalar a los principales problemas. Y su enfado tras el golpe es total. "Es una maniobra muy torpe para un piloto con su experiencia. Le pido disculpas a Gasly, que hizo un gran fin de semana, y a Norris", dijo el italiano. Pero tiene más. "Evaluaré las medidas que podemos tomar. Estoy muy decepcionado", soltó. Habrá sanción y la prensa inglesa, con The Race a la cabeza, adelantó que incluso Briatore valora dejar a Colapinto sin correr en Malasia tras el golpe. Alpine tiene a un tercer piloto con experiencia como es el estonio Aron y el castigo es una posibilidad real. Y se sabe que la mano dura de Briatore es casi una capacidad legendaria de su gestión... Y es lo que pedía Norris. "La FIA tiene que ser estricta, debería estar una carrera castigado", contó. Algo que, por ejemplo, no compraba Max Verstappen. "Si el piloto que causó el accidente es consciente de ello y se disculpa, eso sucede, un pequeño error. Es desafortunado que involucrara tantos pilotos, pero, ¿una carrera de suspensión? Es demasiado”, concluyó. A él le pasó con Ricciardo y tenía sus más y sus menos con Sainz en su era en Toro Rosso. Sabe de lo que habla.

articles.title: Bahrain GP in Malaysia 2026: Dates, schedule, weather, UK start time and how to watch or stream F1 race at Sepang live on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Find out the race-week schedule, weather and how to watch the Bahrain Grand Prix weekend in Malaysia; watch every session of the Bahrain GP from Friday with Sunday's race at 8am, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Bahrain were unable to stage their race in April at their own Sakhir track owing to the conflict in the Middle East but a deal was struck for Malaysia to stage the event instead.

Malaysia last hosted a race in 2017, won by Red Bull's Max Verstappen, with the fast, flowing Sepang circuit considered one of the very best of the newer generation of tracks.

It stages the second leg of the season's first flyaway triple header after George Russell got his title hopes back on track with victory by less than two tenths from Verstappen last time out in Baku.

Kimi Antonelli limited the damage with fifth after crashing in qualifying but saw his lead cut to 66 points with eight rounds remaining, while Lewis Hamilton is 103 points adrift and Lando Norris is 116 points back, but McLaren are expected to be strong at the high-speed Sepang International Circuit.

Malaysia is seven hours ahead of the UK but the scheduling of the key sessions at Sepang means convenient weekend breakfast-time viewing on Sky Sports F1 with Qualifying at 9am on Saturday and the Grand Prix at 8am on Sunday.

Sepang International Circuit track layout

F1's drivers are certainly excited about the sport's return to Sepang - and no wonder.

The sweeping, aerodynamically demanding 3.44-mile layout was the first all-new track designed by F1's now-resident architect Hermann Tilke and quickly made its mark when it staged its inaugural Grand Prix in 1999, with the facility as a whole changing the game for what Formula 1 venues needed to be like in future.

The 15-corner track quickly proved popular with drivers and fans for both the array of impressive medium and high-speed corner sequences, plus the now-common combination of long straights into wide, heavy braking zones.

The long curved run through Turn Three to the Turn Four right-hander, the fast left-right flicks of Turns Five and Six and the sweeping, technical corners of the final sector leading onto the half-mile back straight down to the final turn, a hairpin, all represent key aspects of the lap.

Tropical Malaysia guarantees heat, humidity - and the threat of thunderstorms. Sunny one minute, the scene of a huge downpour the next, F1 teams will have to be sharp with their weather radars this weekend.

articles.title: George Russell: Is Mercedes driver really back after 'Grand Slam' Azerbaijan GP win cut Kimi Antonelli's F1 title lead?
articles.summary: George Russell drove superbly to win the Azerbaijan Grand Prix; Russell reduced his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli's championship lead to 66 points; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia from Friday live on Sky Sports F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix
articles.body:
Russell drove superbly in Baku to claim the first Grand Slam of his career, taking pole position, leading from lights-to-flag on his way to victory, and setting the fastest lap of the race.

The result saw Russell reduce his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli's lead at the top of the world championship to 66 points with eight rounds remaining, ensuring some intrigue remains as the season enters its closing stretch.

Regardless of whether Russell is able to mount a challenge over the remainder of the season, the gulf between him and Antonelli in recent months had begun to create doubts over the 28-year-old's prospects of ever winning a championship while driving alongside the Italian.

There were extenuating circumstances for Antonelli in Baku as he missed a significant chunk of practice with technical issues before crashing out of qualifying to leave himself 16th on the grid, but this was the first time since the opening weekend of the season that Russell had so clearly outperformed him.

Russell has been open in recent months about his difficulty understanding his deficit to Antonelli, which he has largely attributed to the different challenges posed by F1's new cars for 2026, but feels his Baku display was confirmation that a corner has been turned.

Russell said: "I think it's probably my first Grand Slam in Formula 1 and, for sure, the most dominant weekend I've had in my career, so that has come at a really great moment.

"And also to achieve it on a circuit that requires so much commitment and confidence, I'm really proud of because I think it would have been very easy for me to lose the faith this season. Not necessarily about winning the championship, but in terms of my ability, and that never happened.

"I'm very proud of the resilience that I and my close group of engineers have shown during the tough periods this year because there's been a lot of hard work to overcome some of the challenges, to adapt my driving style to suit this new car better.

"And F1 is so tough, you don't get opportunities to practice this, and finally it's coming to me a bit more intuitively than it once did, and I'm gaining confidence."

Russell's victory was made all the more impressive by the fact he had to fend off Red Bull's Max Verstappen in the closing stages having had a big lead taken away by two Safety Car interruptions.

A thrilling race to the chequered flag saw Russell end up just a tenth of a second clear of Verstappen, creating the smallest margin of victory in an F1 race since 2002.

Three-time W Series champion and Sky Sports F1 pundit Jamie Chadwick believes the performance was confirmation that Russell has raised his level.

"He's definitely stepped up," Chadwick said.

"It's a big points gap but I think the championship is still something to be excited about, which for a lot of us coming into this weekend maybe we didn't expect. So that's something to look forward to now."

Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok was particularly impressed by the way Russell fended off four-time world champion Verstappen in the closing stages.

"That last stint from George, he had Verstappen piling the pressure on," Chandhok said. "In some ways that's more satisfying for George.

"It's one thing disappearing off, 10 seconds in the lead and driving by yourself. But winning under pressure will give him more satisfaction."

If Russell really has returned to form, it was good time to do so, with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix having been the first of six races in seven weeks.

The Bahrain Grand Prix, taking place in Malaysia, follows next weekend, with the Singapore Grand Prix completing a triple-header. Then come back-to-back races in the United States, Mexico and Brazil.

The fact Russell needs to take a grid penalty before the end of the season for changing engine stiffens his task, but just proving that he can match Antonelli for pace over the remainder of the year would be a huge psychological boost going into 2027.

Having rarely spoken with any great confidence in recent months, Russell's view on how he sees the battle between himself and Antonelli going forward suggests he has his mojo back.

"There's much less pressure on me than there is him," Russell said. "He's had an incredibly flawless season. Yesterday was probably his first mistake of this whole season in a proper session, qualifying, race, and he still came home in P5 today.

"I didn't really consider myself in this fight for a number of races, purely because my performance wasn't strong enough.

"Now I feel like if the season were to have started today, or since the summer break, I feel very much I would have been able to fight.

"Now I've got this big deficit. It can change quickly. So, I'm not chasing that. I'm chasing to win every race, and what will be, will be."

articles.title: La misma sanción a Colapinto que a Sainz, ¿es justo o equivalente?
articles.standfirst: Franco tendrá cinco puestos de penalización en la parrilla de Sepang, pese a que su acción fue realmente temeraria. En la de Carlos (el sábado) ya no había nadie en pista ni en peligro
articles.summary: Franco tendrá cinco puestos de penalización en la parrilla de Sepang, pese a que su acción fue realmente temeraria. En la de Carlos (el sábado) ya no había nadie en pista ni en peligro
articles.body: Dos acciones muy diferentes.en cuanto a temeridad y peligro real para los afectados... pero la misma sanción al final. Franco Colapinto recibió 10 segundos de penalización por su abordaje salvaje sobre Pierre Gasly en Bakú, que se convierten en 5 posiciones en parrilla para Sepang, la semana que viene, al no poder ser aplicada por el abandono de ayer... Y además habría que sumar los daños ocasionados en los coches. La de Colapinto es una sanción 'tipo', en la que no se contempla la gravedad de lo sucedido, de pasarse ocho pueblos en la frenada y en bloquear e impactar contra un rival, en este caso Gasly, por el lateral del otro monoplaza. Destrozó tres coches, con una factura que superará ampliamente el millones de dólares en reparaciones, sumando los daños propios, los del otro Alpine y los de Lando Norris, al que le gustaría que desapareciese por un tiempo de la parrilla. Curiosamente, es la misma pena que se le aplicó a Carlos Sainz esta sábad,o por supuestamente ignorar las banderas amarillas tras una salida de pista de Lando Norris en la Q3 de la calificación. Las imágenes de a bordo del español muestran una recta despejada de 300 metros, sin nadie en pista y cómo Sainz levantaba el pie del acelerador y luego pisaba de nuevo... cuando no había nadie cruzado o saliendo a la pista. En su caso, se aplicó sin más el tiempo invertido entre dos postes de comisarios de pista y como mejoró el tiempo personal le cayó el máximo (además de 2 puntos en el carnet) sin mirar o calibrar si fue realmente peligroso o no. Y mirando atrás, nada que ver con la mayor sanción de los 15 últimos años, que fue y es la recibida por Fernando Alonso en el GP de Australia de 2024, cuando le cayeron 20 segundos y 2 puntos en la licencia, sin tocar a ningún coche, sino supuestamente despistar a alguien que llegaba más de 20 metros por detrás. Era Russell que volcó él sólo y de cuyo fallo se hizo responsable al asturiano. Franco se puede sentir afortunado por una pena tan liviana, pero Lando, quizá de forma exagerada, pedía sus suspensión por todo el GP de Bahréin que se celebra en Malasia. Algo intermedio hubiera estado bien, algo así como salir en la última posición de la parrilla de Sepang. Y dar las gracias por no haber causado lesiones graves a ningún rival. Hecho: Colisión con el coche 10 en la curva 1. Infracción: Incumplimiento del Apéndice L, Capítulo IV, Artículo 2 d) del Código Deportivo Internacional de la FIA. Decisión: Penalización de 10 segundos convertida en una sanción de 5 posiciones en la parrilla de salida de la próxima carrera en la que participe el piloto. Motivo: Los comisarios revisaron las pruebas de vídeo, los tiempos y las imágenes de la cámara a bordo. Tras la reanudación, COL se acercó a GAS por detrás al llegar a la curva 1. COL frenó demasiado tarde y entró en la curva por el interior a una velocidad que no le permitió tomarla de manera controlada. Se pasó de frenada y colisionó con el lateral izquierdo de GAS; este a su vez impactó contra NOR, provocando el abandono de ambos coches. Los comisarios consideraron que COL fue total o predominantemente responsable de la colisión. Aunque el incidente ocurrió en la primera curva tras la reanudación, no hubo ninguna acción por parte de otro piloto que justificara aplicar el criterio más indulgente habitual para la primera vuelta o la primera curva. La penalización estándar por causar una colisión es de 10 segundos. Dado que COL había abandonado la carrera y, por tanto, no podía cumplir la penalización de tiempo, los comisarios la convirtieron en una sanción de 5 posiciones en la parrilla de salida de la próxima carrera en la que participe el piloto, de conformidad con el Artículo B1.9.6.(e) del Reglamento de F1 de la FIA de 2026.

articles.title: Jorge Prado, rey de América: logra su primer título en los Estados Unidos
articles.standfirst: El gallego se lleva los Playoffs del SuperMotocross, las finales combinadas de los dos grandes campeonatos americanos
articles.summary: El gallego se lleva los Playoffs del SuperMotocross, las finales combinadas de los dos grandes campeonatos americanos
articles.body: La vida cambia rápido, de golpe, y el deporte ofrece segundas oportunidades cuando las puertas parecen cerradas a cal y canto. Esa ley de las personas la puede aplicar Jorge Prado, el mejor representante de la historia de España en el motocross. Que se fue a los Estados Unidos de América, donde los campeonatos son una religión, tras ser todo en Europa y poder ser considerado como uno de los mejores de todos los tiempos. Cayó, se hizo daño... y recordará el final del curso 2026 como el que le encumbra. Ya es campeón. Prado cerró con éxito en Rigedale, una zona residencial en Misuri, el título del Campeonato del Mundo de SuperMotocross. Es un formato nacido como un Playoff final entre los reyes del Supercross de inicios de año y del ProMotocross, el campeonato al aire libre del periodo estival. Y tras ser tercero en Colombus y primero en Carson, el gallego pasó al ataque en la gran final con un quinto puesto en la primera carrera y victoria en la ronda decisiva. No tuvo que preocuparse en exceso por Haiden Deegan, al que batió en la última carrera y dejó con la miel en los labios pese a ser el vencedor de la ronda en conjunto. "Esto es lo que los campeones hacen. Siempre vuelven", recalcaba el lucense ya con su 1 estampado. Tenía que enviar un mensaje de reivindicación, pues su primer año (2025) al completo en los Estados Unidos fue malo, se llenó de lesiones y salió por la puerta de atrás de una fábrica de Kawasaki que jamás le entendió. Volvió a su casa, KTM, y la regularidad ha sido su arma durante toda la temporada. "Hace un año no tenía una moto para correr... Pero conseguimos prepararnos para trabajar cada fin de semana y conseguí volver a mi nivel. Estoy muy feliz por el título. Ya era un cuatro veces campeón por algo y todo es posible", explicó. La historia de Prado es, claro, la del niño prodigio. La del chico joven que desde el inicio tiene cualidades. Pero también el que tiene alejarse de casa y de los suyos para trabajar. Así se mudó a Bélgica siendo un niño y así buscaba también el éxito en los Estados Unidos. "He dejado todo atrás. Cambié mi vida de Europa. Y el año pasado pasé mi peor momento, pero trabajé mucho y conseguí con el equipo cosas increíbles porque todos íbamos en la misma dirección", recalcó. No sin olvidar que sufrió en la primera parte del último fin de semana, pero sacando más a su KTM. En su palmarés ya siempre quedará esa chapa de campeón en los Estados Unidos, el mundo que respira motocross. Consiguiendo lo que muchos no se han atrevido y con ansias de buscar las coronas de los dos campeonatos en los que volverá a tomar la salida en 2027, el SuperCross y Pro Motocross. Ahora ya nadie duda de Jorge Prado.

articles.title: Alpine condemn online abuse since Franco Colapinto three-car Azerbaijan GP crash with Pierre Gasly, Lando Norris
articles.summary: Franco Colapinto's mistake at first Safety Car restart in Baku led to chain-reaction accident that also saw team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris drop out; Alpine condemn social media abuse aimed at all sides seen since crash
articles.body:
Alpine driver Colapinto triggered the accident in the Baku race's first Safety Car restart when he locked his brakes into the first corner and hit the side of team-mate Gasly, who was sent straight into Norris' McLaren on his outside.

"Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport," Alpine said as part of a statement issued on Sunday.

All three drivers retired with car damage, with Colapinto apologising to his team-mate, Alpine and Norris for what he admitted had been a "big mistake".

Colapinto will take a five-place grid penalty at this coming week's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia in lieu of the 10-second time penalty he was unable to serve in the race as he had retired.

Speaking in the immediate aftermath of the incident, a Norris said that drivers who cause incidents like Colapinto did should be banned for one race . The McLaren driver also said "there are some drivers who shouldn't be in Formula 1, to be honest".

Alpine have previously spoken out to condemn online hate from some fans seen following incidents in which Colapinto, who has a big following in Argentina, was involved.

'It has become a regular occurrence and cannot be condoned' - Alpine's statement in full

"As a team, we feel it's necessary to speak out once more about the hate and abuse online following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

"Not only aimed at one of our own drivers, but also members of the Formula One community, including media, and to our racing counterparts who we respect, admire, and revel competing against in the pinnacle of motorsport.

"Mistakes happen when racing at the limit and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments.

"Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport.

"As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula One, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned.

"We know as a proud participant and stakeholder in the sport, we hold a responsibility to speak out and also help support in finding a solution. We will continue to work closely with the championship promoter and rights-holder, and the governing body to discuss ways in which to tackle online abuse and encourage healthy sporting rivalry, which Formula One is renowned for and what makes it so special."

Briatore: I will consider what course of action should be taken with Colapinto

Speaking on Saturday evening about the on-track incident itself, Alpine executive advisor Flavio Briatore said he would take time "reflect on what course of action should be taken" after Colapinto's "very poor" error.

Gasly had been running a strong seventh at the time, with Colapinto 10th, and the incident cost Alpine what stood as seven points overall.

With both Alpines and Norris having dropped out ahead of him, Arvid Lindblad instead came through late in the race to finish seventh and stretch Racing Bulls' lead over Alpine in the fight for fifth place in the Constructors' Championship to 15 points with a scheduled eight rounds left.

Speaking in Alpine's official press release issued after the race, Briatore said: "Obviously I'm extremely disappointed with the outcome of today's race, knowing we lost valuable points in the championship fight.

"These sorts of incidents shouldn't happen, particularly when we were running well with both cars in point-scoring positions.

"I feel very sorry for the team and for Pierre who did a great job all weekend and my apologies also go to Lando [Norris] and McLaren for ruining their race.

"I know that Franco has taken full responsibility for it, as he should; in fact he braked far too late considering the context of the race and the safety car restart. It was a very poor move for a driver of his experience.

"I want to take time to reflect on it and consider what course of action should be taken, so we can learn from it and avoid such a situation in future."

'That's too harsh' - Russell, Verstappen, Hadjar disagree with race ban suggestion

Saturday's top-three finishers in Baku were asked in the post-race press conference about Norris' comments but all agreed that banning a driver for a race for such an incident would be a step too far.

Baku race winner George Russell said: "I think that's too harsh, personally.

"I think Safety Car restarts, cold tyres, a very small mistake can have big consequences.

"And from what I saw today, that's what it looked like. It was a small error that had a big consequence. I think, personally, race bans should come from drivers intentionally doing something very dangerous and very reckless. So I think it was unfortunate."

Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who finished a close second in the race, added: "I think as long as, of course, the driver that caused it is aware of what he did, right, and apologised.

"And, I mean, yeah, that happens. I mean, like, a small mistake or misjudgement, you lock up, it's on the inside, low grip, and, of course, then I guess a bit unfortunate that it involves so many cars.

"But, yeah, unfortunate, happens, and it's not nice, I think. Not nice for anyone involved, right? But like George said, I think, yeah, a race ban probably is a bit much."

Third-place finisher Isack Hadjar agreed with Russell and Verstappen, especially as he felt there were mitigating circumstances in the incident.

"I think the track is not good enough," said the Red Bull driver.

"You move out of the racing line, it starts to be very bumpy. It's hard to generate temperature behind the Safety Car, it's going quite slowly.

"So then, yeah, you just overdo it and then it has big, big consequences. So, I think, yeah, a race ban is way too harsh."

Andrea Stella, Norris' McLaren team boss, said they trusted the stewards to make the right decisions, adding that drivers should also be expected to race with "a certain degree of just common sense".

"It's a complex matter," said Stella before Colapinto's converted grid drop was officially confirmed.

"I guess this is being reviewed by the stewards as we speak, pretty much. I'm sure it will be reviewed by Flavio as well. I'm not sure which one is going to be harsher for whoever caused the problem.

"I think, independently of the dissuasion that you can have because of the penalty, I think when you drive in Formula 1 and you are approaching Turn 1 in Baku and you have seen so many videos of the past, you just should be capitalising on this experience that you should be having as a Formula 1 driver.

"The consequence in this case, which I'm sure, is a shame for Alpine for both drivers, and there's a penalty for other drivers.

"Definitely the penalty should take into account that there are some circuits in which you have to use extra prudency, and there's a full history of problems that happened like this, especially in a street circuit where there's no way to use the runoff area to somehow mitigate the consequences of somebody running onto you.

"We trust the stewards, their approach, but above all, we should trust the drivers that they apply a certain degree of just common sense I would say while driving."
